newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish Life buys U.S. firm for $163 million.
newsitem.headline: Irish Life buys U.S. firm for $163 million.

text.p: Irish Life Plc said on Thursday that it had agreed to buy Illinois-based Guarantee Reserve Life Assurance Company for $163 million, its largest acquisition to date.
The Irish life assurance and investment company said the acquisition of the privately-owned U.S. firm would be funded from its existing resources and from debt financing.
"This is a very significant acquisition which advances our strategic direction appreciably, not only in the U.S. but in the group as a whole," managing director David Kingston told a news conference.
He said the acquisition, which involves goodwill of $17 million, represented excellent value and should be earnings enhancing in 1997.
Irish Life hopes to complete the acquisition by March 31 and expects it to contribute over four million Irish pounds ($6.6 million) to earnings next year.
The acquisition should also help Irish Life realise its aim of having $1.0 billion in U.S. premium revenues by the year 2000 and one million U.S. customers by the year 2005, Kingston said.
Guarantee Reserve has an innovative marketing and distribution approach which can open up new growth opportunities for Irish Life's existing U.S. businesses.

The U.S. firm is a lead generation specialist and its database can be used to help in generating customers for Irish Life's other U.S. operations which include Iowa-based Interstate and Boston-based First Variable, Kingston said.
Following the acquisition, group premium income is expected to rise to $408 million or 33 percent of group total, based on 1995 figures, from 27 percent.
Guarantee Reserve is licensed to write life assurance and accidental and health business in 47 states plus Washington DC. It has 175 employees and around 340,000 policyholders.
It focuses on providing risk cover for older age groups and its current target market is low to middle income groups.

Kingston said the company's growth capacity is significant as the older age group is scheduled to reach 60 million in the U.S. by the year 2000 while less than 40 percent of the company's target market own a life assurance policy.

Guarantee Reserve, which had premium income of $81.8 million in the year ended December 31, 1995 and $46.1 million in the half-year to June, also has the opportunity to grow its share among mid-market and lower age groups, he said.
The move was welcomed in the market.
"It's good that they're doing something and the acquisition is earnings enhancing. It's being viewed positively and the share price has already gone up a few pence," one dealer said.
Irish Life's share price rose three pence to 272 and was at 271 by 1500 GMT. ($ = 0.603 Irish Pounds)
